plan: This is a single-round auction. Since all bidders are rational, and values are private, the optimal bidding strategy is to bid slightly below your value. Given the values are between 0 and 49, and other bidders are rational, I will bid a fraction of my value to ensure a profit if I win. A reasonable starting point is to bid around 80% of my value. So, 0.8 * 30 = 24. I will bid $23.9 to try and win if the other bidders also bid rationally.

This is a single-round auction. The optimal bidding strategy in a single-round, second-price sealed-bid auction is to bid slightly below your true value. This is because bidding your exact value leaves you vulnerable to losing to a slightly higher bid, and bidding higher than your value risks paying more than the item is worth. I will bid slightly below my value to maximize my expected profit.

I will use the Nash Equilibrium strategy. With 3 bidders, the optimal bidding strategy is to bid two-thirds of my value. My value is $24, so I will bid (2/3) * 24 = $16. This strategy assumes the other bidders are also rational and using a similar strategy.
